Duration::sizes¶

Back to Duration API Reference

Signature¶

auto Duration::sizes() const

What It Tells You¶

sizes() exposes the logical extent of each axis in outermost-to-innermost order. A scalar reports [], not [1]; [1] is a one-element vector.

The result is a borrowed, read-only range backed by the Duration handle. It is cheap to inspect but should not outlive the Duration. Construct an owning std::vector<std::int64_t> when shape metadata must be stored independently. Shape describes arrangement only; it does not encode units, validity, or lane values.

Returns¶

A borrowed range whose length equals dim(). The product of its extents equals numel().

Examples¶

Example 1. Scalar, vector, matrix, and rank-three shapes.

auto shape = [](const pluss::Duration& d) {
  std::cout << '[';
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < d.sizes().size(); ++i) {
    if (i) std::cout << ',';
    std::cout << d.sizes()[i];
  }
  std::cout << "]\n";
};

shape(pluss::duration::seconds(90));
shape(pluss::duration::minutes({15,30,45}));
shape(pluss::duration::hours({1,2,3,4}, {2,2}));
shape(pluss::duration::nanos({1,2,3,4}, {2,1,2}));

Output¶

[]
[3]
[2,2]
[2,1,2]

Example 2. Preserve a zero-length axis.

const auto empty = pluss::duration::zeros({2,0,3});
std::cout << "dim=" << empty.dim() << " numel=" << empty.numel() << " sizes=[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < empty.sizes().size(); ++i) {
  if (i) std::cout << ',';
  std::cout << empty.sizes()[i];
}
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

dim=3 numel=0 sizes=[2,0,3]

Example 3. Take an owning copy for independent storage.

const auto value = pluss::duration::hours({1,2,3,4}, {2,2});
const std::vector<std::int64_t> owned(value.sizes().begin(), value.sizes().end());
std::cout << "rank=" << owned.size()
          << " rows=" << owned[0] << " columns=" << owned[1] << "\n";

Output¶

rank=2 rows=2 columns=2

See Also¶

  • dim: number of extents.

  • numel: product of extents.

  • host: owning copy of lane data rather than shape metadata.
